lines.ruling: Ruling: scope; f1040 p. 1, "If joint return, spouse's first name", and Filing Status, "Married filing jointly (even if only one had income)". Ruled by reading: the household triage cannot be rerun (triage.py refuses the form because an earlier pass names household.widowed_2025, renamed household.widowed_this_year per tools/year_free_names.json) and the record on disk predates the redraft, so no triage counts are cited. The reply's test (one taxpayer entry; a spouse entry exactly on a joint return) is the complement of the project's household.roster_ok by De Morgan's laws; the project's line also carries roster_ok's entry checks, the filer under 16 (amb.2025.filer_under_16) and the impossible birth year (household.birth_year_bad, docs/provisional/DECISIONS.md section 2), which the reply bypasses, as ruled before. Project stands.

Ruling: representation; i8889 p. 4, "If you and your spouse each have separate HSAs, complete a separate Form 8889 for each". Both count persons with a Form 8889 and test for two (0 < n against 1 <= n on an integral count). No difference. executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/household.json`; 1,565 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 235 partial records; 2,300 comparisons): 2,300 of 2,300 agree; none; on returns the full interview completes: none. Project stands.

Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 40, Step 1, question 2. "No filer without a valid SSN" against "every filer has one": the same test. No difference. executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/household.json`; 1,565 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 235 partial records; 2,300 comparisons): 2,300 of 2,300 agree; none; on returns the full interview completes: none. Project stands.

Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 17, Before you begin: "If you want to claim the credit for other dependents, you, and your spouse if filing jointly, must have either an SSN or ITIN issued on or before the due date of your 2025 return (including extensions)"; p. 19, Step 5, question 1 (an ITIN applied for by the due date counts). Both sides now read the new helper person.tin_or_itin_applied (ruled in the person log). The project tests that the count of persons with an SSN or ITIN (or an ITIN applied for) equals the number of persons on the return; the reply tests that the count of persons without one is zero: the same test on every definite answer. The project line's where-test changed only by reading that helper in place of the former any-test. executable-triage-v2 (`.transcription/triage/2025/household.json`, pass 7073fcafb61a; 1,702 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 247 partial records; 2,449 comparisons): 2,449 of 2,449 agree; no difference (observed equivalence on that sample). As the prior rulings on this line. Project stands.

Ruling: representation; project retained. i1040gi p. 17, Before you begin: "If you are filing a joint return, only one spouse is required to have a valid SSN to be eligible for the CTC and ACTC. The other spouse must have either an SSN or ITIN". The reply counts the taxpayer's and the spouse's entries by role; the project counts every person, and any roster other than one entry for you and, on a joint return, one for your spouse is refused at Form 1040 line 1a (household.roster_bad), so the counts agree within scope, as ruled before. The project's person count reads person.work_ssn_or_tin, now a choice on person.tin first (owner, T-264), so it is unknown on records that answer work_ssn and withhold tin (classm.s1a.1: no dependent, the line is not read on that return); the reply's unknowns withhold the filing status (stage21.choose.eic_limit_status_unanswered). No value differs. Reviewed again line-scoped as a T-150 sibling refresh (the readers of the gate-wave follow-up's rewritten lines, BUG-0466/0471, T-264; this line itself is unchanged). executable-triage-v2 (.transcription/triage/2025/household.json; 1,747 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 247 partial records): 2,484 of 2,520 comparisons agree; differences {"candidate-unknown": 3, "project-unknown": 33}; on completed returns {"project-unknown": 5}.

Ruling: representation; project retained. The project tests 0 < count and the reply 1 <= count; for a count the two are the same test, as ruled before. No difference. Reviewed again line-scoped as a T-150 sibling refresh (the readers of the gate-wave follow-up's rewritten lines, BUG-0466/0471, T-264; this line itself is unchanged). executable-triage-v2 (.transcription/triage/2025/household.json; 1,747 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 247 partial records): 2,520 of 2,520 comparisons agree; differences {}; on completed returns none.

Ruling: representation; Pub. 501 Marital Status; i1040gi p. 13, Single. Both are true for a married filing status (mfj, mfs, qss) and household.ever_married for single or head of household; the reply writes it as an any() that reads household.ever_married raw, which the project asks only of a single or head of household filer. Same value wherever the reply's input is asked. Ruled by reading: the triage record predates this reply (pass de16cc0a21be not in .transcription/triage/2025/household.json).

Ruling: model error; p501 p. 6, Marital Status: "If your spouse died during the year, you are considered married for the whole year for filing status purposes" is a filing-status rule, which the project carries in household.widowed_this_year and household.joint_unmarried; the interface itself is "Married at the end of 2025", and its readers use that year-end fact (i8889 p. 6, Line 3 Limitation Chart, "If, at the end of 2025, you were unmarried and age 55 or older"; f8889.sf_married, "Married at the end of 2025"). The reply makes a filer whose spouse died in 2025 married, changing the year-end status read by Form 8889 and by the head of household test, and reads household.married_dec31 and household.spouse_died_this_year where the interview asks neither (a never-married single or head of household filer). Ruled by reading: no household triage (triage.py refuses the form because an earlier pass names the renamed household.widowed_2025; the record on disk predates the redraft). Project stands.

Ruling: model error; i1040s8812 p. 2, Form 8862 may be required, "you must attach Form 8862 to your tax return to claim the CTC, ACTC, or ODC unless an exception applies". As the earlier rulings on this line found of earlier replies, the reply reads household.credit_disallowed on returns where the project does not: the project asks it only when the return claims one of the credits (household.credit_disallowed_if_claimed), and the reply tests the answer first, with a claim test of its own (a count of dependents). Its note says the pages do not define this interface. Re-reviewed because household.credit_disallowed was reworded so that it reads correctly with and without the spouse phrase (wording only; no expression changed). executable-triage-v2 (`.transcription/triage/2025/household.json`, pass 219699d4eb98; 1,767 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 226 partial records): 1,842 of 2,493 comparisons agree; differences by kind {"candidate-unknown": 7, "project-refuses": 556, "project-unknown": 88}; on completed returns 5 candidate-unknown, each for household.credit_disallowed where the project is false (for example classm.s8812.4.deepseek); no value difference. The other differences are on refused or incomplete returns. No change to the data.

Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 43, "You must file Form 8862 if your EIC for a year after 1996 was reduced or disallowed" (the form goes with a claim of the credit). The one completed value witness is the one of the earlier rulings on this line, f2.t101.credit_disallowed_eic_zero (project false, reply true): the reply tests the answer with eic.eligible, which its note says is "assumed to mean that the filer meets the EIC steps" and is used "rather than the credit amount", so it is true on a Yes answer where no earned income credit is claimed. Re-reviewed because household.credit_disallowed was reworded so that it reads correctly with and without the spouse phrase (wording only; no expression changed). executable-triage-v2 (`.transcription/triage/2025/household.json`, pass 219699d4eb98; 1,767 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 226 partial records): 1,952 of 2,493 comparisons agree; differences by kind {"candidate-unknown": 4, "project-refuses": 458, "project-unknown": 78, "value": 1}; on completed returns 1 value (above) and 1 candidate-unknown for household.credit_disallowed where the project is false (classm.person.22). The other differences are on refused or incomplete returns. No change to the data.

Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 14, Head of Household, "Check the 'Head of household' box only if you are unmarried (or considered unmarried) and either Test 1 or Test 2 applies"; Pub. 501 p. 6, "If your spouse died during the year, you are considered married for the whole year". The reply's tests are the project's: dependent.hoh_test1 (Test 1), dependent.hoh_test2 with household.home_cost (Test 2, the project's test2_met), married_dec31 and not considered_unmarried (the project's household.unmarried false). It also folds in a spouse who died in 2025, which the project refuses at the same Form 1040 status line through household.widowed_this_year (f1040.yaml refuses on hoh_fails and widowed_this_year side by side), and it reads married_dec31 and considered_unmarried raw where the project gates them. Same refusal outcome. Ruled by reading: the triage record predates this reply (pass de16cc0a21be).

Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 13, Married Filing Jointly: "You can choose married filing jointly as your filing status if any of the following apply ... Your spouse died in 2025 and you didn't remarry in 2025"; the interface is "Filing as single or head of household although your spouse died in 2025", the refusal at Form 1040 line 12e. The reply drops the filing-status guard, so the gate is true on a valid death-year joint (or separate) return, refusing it, as the earlier replies to this line (household.widowed_2025) were ruled. Ruled by reading: no household triage (triage.py refuses the form because an earlier pass names the renamed household.widowed_2025; the record on disk predates the redraft). Project stands.

Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 23, Community Property States, and p501 p. 6 (part-year marriage in a community property state; Form 8958, Pub. 555). Both are true for a filer not filing jointly who lived in a community property state, was not married at the end of 2025 and was married there for part of 2025. The project asks household.cp_married only where a marriage is possible (marriage_possible: not a never-married single or head of household filer) and reads year-end marriage through household.married; the reply reads household.married_dec31 and household.cp_married directly, so it differs only on records where the interview asks neither. Ruled by reading: no household triage (triage.py refuses the form because an earlier pass names the renamed household.widowed_2025; the record on disk predates the redraft). Project stands.

Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 23, Community Property States; p501 p. 6. As the prior ruling (`.transcription/archive/before-catalog-refresh-2026-11-03/`): the reply tests household.rdp alone, dropping the nonjoint and community-property guards, so it asks the answer on every return (262 completed candidate-unknowns, for example classm.f8889.1.deepseek). Not a tax-value disagreement. executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/household.json`; 1,565 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 235 partial records; 2,300 comparisons): 611 of 2,300 agree; 1,689 candidate-unknown; on returns the full interview completes: 262 candidate-unknown. Project stands.

Ruling: model error; read without triage (triage.py refuses the log: an old line-scoped pass, 7073fcafb61a, names household.widowed_2025, which the form no longer compares). The changed alternative is MFS: the project refuses a separate return only when the filer was not married at the end of 2025 and no spouse died in 2025 (household.joint_unmarried); the reply refuses every MFS filer not married on Dec 31, so it refuses a 2025 widow filing separately. p501 p. 6, Spouse died during the year: "If your spouse died during the year, you are considered married for the whole year for filing status purposes"; i1040gi p. 14 allows MFS to a married filer. The project is right. The reply's other differences fold in cases other gates refuse (a 2025 death on a single return: household.widowed_2025; HOH tests: household.hoh_fails; QSS: household.qss_fails), as the prior rounds ruled (scope).

Ruling: representation; read without triage (triage.py refuses the log, see filing_status_conflict). On MFS both read household.mfs_living == apart_all_year. Off MFS the project reads the year parameter household.mfs_living_else (together_late), so the test is false, and the reply's conjunction with status mfs is false too; the reply only reads the gated input ungated. Equal on every status (i1040gi p. 31, Line 6d; amb.2025.mfs_lived_apart).

Ruling: representation; read without triage (see filing_status_conflict). On MFS both are apart_last6 or apart_all_year (the reply's note picks the IRS condition 'lived apart for the last 6 months', which the all-year value also meets, as the project does). Off MFS both are false (project: together_late from household.mfs_living_else; reply: conjunction with status mfs). i1040gi p. 15, Married persons who live apart; p. 44, Special rule for separated spouses.

Ruling: representation; read without triage (see filing_status_conflict). On MFS both are household.community_property; on every other status the project gives household.no (false) and the reply's conjunction with status mfs gives false. The reply's note leaves registered domestic partners to household.rdp, as the project does (household.rdp_community_property). i1040gi p. 14, Married Filing Separately, "Different rules apply to people in community property states; see Pub. 555"; amb.2025.mfs_community_property.
